details.description: Nova-2 Voicemail is a domain-specific variant of Deepgram's Nova-2 speech-to-text model, tuned for low-bandwidth audio clips with a single speaker; Deepgram's documentation describes it as derived from the Nova-2 Phonecall model. It shares the Nova-2 generation's architecture, which Deepgram says expands on Nova-1 with speech-specific Transformer optimizations, advanced data curation, and multi-stage training that improve word error rate, entity recognition, punctuation, and capitalization. Deepgram's docs currently list Nova-2 as a supported, non-legacy generation, with the newer Nova-3 generation recommended for most general transcription use cases.
advantages: Purpose-built for low-bandwidth, single-speaker audio and derived from Deepgram's Phonecall model, per Deepgram's documentation.

Built on Deepgram's Nova-2 architecture, which the company says adds speech-specific Transformer optimizations, advanced data curation, and multi-stage training that reduce word error rate versus the earlier Nova-1 generation.
disadvantages: Supports English audio only (en, en-US), per Deepgram's language table.
Deepgram's newer Nova-3 generation is now its recommended default for most transcription, though Nova-3 does not currently offer a dedicated voicemail domain variant to directly replace this one.
use_cases: Transcribing voicemail messages and other low-bandwidth, single-speaker audio clips.

notes: No word-error-rate or other accuracy figures specific to the voicemail variant were published; the 'speech-specific optimizations' description on developers.deepgram.com/docs/model applies to the whole Nova-2 generation, not a voicemail-specific benchmark, so it is described as architecture context rather than a measured result for this variant. Catalog facts (empty deprecation_date, audio_input->text_output, /v1/audio/transcriptions endpoint) are consistent with the maker's docs. Nova-2 is not under Deepgram's 'Legacy Models' heading (only Nova/Enhanced/Base are), so it is not described as deprecated.
